value.hook: Open before writing anything that ends a wait by notifying someone else (prime, Telegram, fallback), or that retries a send after a crash
value.title: Settling a result once across channels (F139, #197 rounds 1-3)

sections.name: body
sections.value:
What four review rounds on #197 (the orphaned bg final turn) required. Each one was a BLOCK until fixed:
- Read the saved settlement FIRST on every look, before reclassifying the owner or the target. Otherwise, after a crash, a revived owner or a now-gone prime gets a second delivery on another channel.
- Prime leg: the delivery ledger (`delivery.admitted(seat, id)`) decides, not `accept`'s Result. `accept` can admit and then fail its audit publish (`DeliveryAuditFailed`). Re-check admission after ANY error; if the re-check itself fails, keep the route and retry (braked), never fall back on an unknown.
- A recorded route is not a licence to wake: re-check the prime's warmth on replay. Cold or gone switches to Telegram, recorded first.
- Telegram leg: the queue's dedupe covers only pending and running rows, so a completed send can be re-sent. The orphan record, the jobs row and the notified mark go in ONE sqlite transaction (`SqliteBackground::settle_by_telegram`; the background pool is the queue's pool in production). No commit flag plus undo: an undo can fail.
- Brakes must hold on the failure path too: a failed settle, or a failed log-tail read, sets the next look 60 s out. Filter waiting rows in the pending QUERY (`pending_skipping`), and keep it the only brake so a mutant can show it working.
- Do optional work (reading the log tail) only after routing; an orphan doesn't need it.
- Render every seat or path in the notice (`SeatId::rendered`, `render::caller_text`), including in the shared Telegram header (sidecars `prefixed_text_parts`). Fake fixture seats like "owner" render as `invalid (5 chars)`.
- The fake registry's `tombstone()` stamps a sequence number, not a time. Put a descriptor with a real `tombstoned_at` instead.
- In AGENTS.md terms, name each check a policy (it decides the outcome) or a brake (it only spares work).
